A $20 Million Montana Retreat Keeps His Family Coming Back for More
 
Plus: Crested Butte bucks a ski-market slump, and a look inside the East Coast’s most expensive ski town
 
By Kerry Barger
 
 
ALYSSA FREESE FOR WSJ
 

This is an edition of the WSJ Homes newsletter, a weekly guide to luxurious properties, celebrity homes, interior design and the housing market. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

When I finally got my own room growing up, I was allowed to choose the paint color for the walls. You could say I had slightly less input than Roy Carroll’s daughters, who were given carte blanche to design custom suites inside his $20 million Montana home.

 

The project began when the billionaire developer’s wife, Vanessa, and three daughters—now 31, 34, and 36—fell in love with a ski-in, ski-out lot at the upscale Yellowstone Club near Big Sky. Carroll bought the property for $4.5 million in 2018 and built an eight-bedroom “mountain-traditional” home featuring elements that are “all-out Montana,” according to lead architect Corey Kelly, a partner at Bozeman-based Locati Architects.

 

Along with a saloon featuring a life-size replica of John Wayne and a mine-shaft-style wine cave, the home includes individual suites for Carroll’s three daughters. Each comes with a bathroom, walk-in closet and fireplace.

 

The suites vary drastically and reflect the personality of each daughter. “I wanted them to feel like they had ownership,” said Roy.

 
 
Carroll Snyder’s suite has leather-wrapped nightstands, timber ceilings and a cowhide-upholstered headboard and footboard. ALYSSA FREESE FOR WSJ
 

While many western ski markets are slowing down this year, Crested Butte, Colo., continues to boom, according to agent Channing Boucher of LIV Sotheby’s International Realty. There, affluent newcomers with tens of millions to spend are building custom homes equipped with plunge pools and oxygenation systems.

 

“The wealth factor has completely changed,” said Boucher. “That’s what we’re all kind of grappling with now.”

 

We also visit another major ski destination: the 05672 ZIP Code in Stowe, nestled in Vermont’s Green Mountains. This small community has the priciest residential real estate of any major East Coast alpine ski destination.

This Small Mountain Community Has the East Coast’s Most Expensive Ski Homes

What’s the Deal?

 
 
MIKE HELFRICH
 

Tennis great John McEnroe is hardly known for his mellow temperament. But his house in Malibu, Calif., he said, has been a calming force. Now, McEnroe and his wife, singer-songwriter Patty Smyth, are listing the beachfront property for $35 million.

 

In California’s San Jacinto Mountains, a harvest-gold, 1960s flying-saucer home—one of the world’s few remaining “Futuro” houses—is hitting the market for $1.495 million.

 

Lumber Liquidators founder Tom Sullivan is listing his 122.5-acre Tennessee ranch, which includes a six-bedroom lodge, for $34.8 million.

 

Want to see more deals? Sign up for our Mansion Deals email alert to have the biggest and best luxury home sales and listings delivered to your inbox.

 
 
 

The Luxe Life

 
 
JENNY RISHER
 

Alice Cooper drew fashion inspiration from an unlikely source. “I saw surreal artist Salvador Dali on ‘The Tonight Show’ and realized that looking eccentric was cool.”

 
 
 

House of the Week

 
 
DUNE LAKE STUDIO
 

The owner of WSJ’s House of the Week isn’t your typical architect. “I’m like a little kid in a candy shop,” says Chris Stoyles, who created a colorful compound along Florida’s scenic 30A highway.

 

The home, which pops with vibrant colors like Barbie pink, avocado green and yellow, is packed with fun features, including a mini-golf course, arcade museum and treehouse.
